title: Localized and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer

steps.tx: Prostate cancer histological grading uses the International Society of Urological Pathology ISUP **Grade Groups** 1 to 5, which correlate more accurately with clinical outcomes than traditional **Gleason score** totals. Grade Group 1 corresponds to Gleason 3+3=6, Grade Group 2 to Gleason 3+4=7, Grade Group 3 to Gleason 4+3=7, Grade Group 4 to Gleason 8, and Grade Group 5 to Gleason 9-10.

steps.tx: **Multiparametric MRI mpMRI** of the prostate evaluated by **PI-RADS** version **2.1** improves clinically significant cancer detection while reducing overdiagnosis of indolent tumours. Scores range from 1 for highly unlikely to 5 for highly likely clinically significant cancer, incorporating T2-weighted imaging for the transition zone and diffusion-weighted imaging DWI with apparent diffusion coefficient ADC mapping for the peripheral zone.

steps.tx: Radical prostatectomy with bilateral pelvic **lymphadenectomy** is a curative-intent surgical standard for intermediate and high-risk localized prostate cancer. Extended pelvic **lymphadenectomy** removes external iliac, obturator, and internal iliac nodal packets, providing accurate pathological nodal staging and identifying micrometastatic disease requiring early multimodal adjuvant or salvage intervention.

steps.tx: After radical prostatectomy, PSA should become **undetectable within about 6 weeks**. Persistent measurable PSA suggests residual or recurrent disease. In recurrence, PSMA PET helps localise disease, but it cannot detect low-volume microscopic spread, so a negative scan does not exclude nodal involvement. Serial PSA monitoring follows the patient after treatment.

steps.tx: Definitive **external beam radiation** therapy combined with 18 to 36 months of long-term androgen deprivation therapy is the standard nonsurgical curative treatment for high-risk localized prostate cancer. In randomized trials from RTOG and EORTC, adding long-term **androgen deprivation therapy** to high-dose external beam radiation significantly prolonged metastasis-free survival and overall survival compared to radiation alone.

left.title: Standard ADT + Radiotherapy (STAMPEDE Control)
items: EBRT plus 3 years of GnRH agonist/antagonist monotherapy
Targeted to prostate and elective whole-pelvis lymph nodes
6-year metastasis-free survival 69%
6-year overall survival 77%

right.title: Abiraterone + Prednisone Intensification
items: EBRT + 3 years ADT + 2 years Abiraterone (1000 mg) + Prednisone (5 mg)
Dual testicular and adrenal/intratumoural androgen suppression
6-year metastasis-free survival 82% (HR 0.53, p < 0.0001)
6-year overall survival 86% (HR 0.60, statistically superior)

steps.tx: The **STAMPEDE trial** established that adding 2 years of **abiraterone acetate plus prednisolone** to long-term androgen deprivation therapy and radiotherapy in very-high-risk or node-positive localized prostate cancer significantly improves metastasis-free survival. In the **STAMPEDE trial**, 6-year metastasis-free survival improved from 69% to 82%, confirming the benefit of upfront next-generation hormonal intensification.

left.title: Post-Radical Prostatectomy Recurrence
items: Total surgical extirpation removes all healthy prostate epithelium
Expected post-operative PSA is undetectable (< 0.1 ng/mL)
Recurrence defined as PSA >= 0.2 ng/mL confirmed by second test
Early salvage radiotherapy is most effective at PSA < 0.5 ng/mL

right.title: Post-Radiotherapy Recurrence (Phoenix Definition)
items: Healthy irradiated prostate parenchyma remains in situ
Residual benign tissue produces baseline nadir PSA level
Recurrence defined as PSA nadir + 2.0 ng/mL
Date of failure marked at time nadir + 2 is documented

steps.tx: Biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy is defined as PSA 0.2 ng/mL or higher, warranting early **salvage radiotherapy**, whereas after radiotherapy it is defined by the Phoenix criteria of **nadir plus 2 ng/mL**. Initiating **salvage radiotherapy** to the prostatic bed at PSA levels under 0.5 ng/mL optimizes cure rates while preventing distant metastatic progression.

steps.tx: Prostate-specific membrane antigen **PSMA PET-CT** provides superior diagnostic accuracy compared to conventional CT and bone scintigraphy in high-risk localized staging and biochemical recurrence in the **proPSMA** trial. In proPSMA, gallium-68 PSMA-11 PET-CT exhibited a 27% absolute improvement in accuracy over conventional imaging, detecting occult nodal and distant skeletal metastases at sub-nanogram PSA levels.

steps.tx: Dynamic kinetics of serum prostate-specific antigen distinguish indolent local failure from aggressive distant metastatic progression. PSA kinetics guide systemic therapy in biochemical recurrence, where a rapid **PSA doubling time** of less than 9 months or velocity over 2 ng/mL/year strongly predicts distant **metastatic progression and cancer-specific death**. Patients with rapid PSA doubling times require early imaging with PSMA-PET and consideration of early systemic hormonal therapy.

left.title: Indolent Biochemical Recurrence
items: PSA doubling time > 12 months
Interval to recurrence > 3 years post-definitive treatment
Low Gleason score (Grade Group 1-2) at initial pathology
Consistent with isolated local anastomotic relapse

right.title: Aggressive Biochemical Recurrence
items: PSA doubling time < 9 months
Interval to recurrence < 12 months post-prostatectomy
High Gleason score (Grade Group 4-5) or seminal vesicle invasion
High risk of distant micrometastatic osseous dissemination
